<|begin_of_text|> Cody Simpson is an Australian pop and R&B singer-songwriter who began his career as a child pop musician, gaining early recognition through his time with School Boy Records. Born and raised on the Gold Coast, he later became an Australian expatriate in the United States, where he continued to develop his music under Atlantic Records. Known for his smooth vocals and youthful charisma, Simpson blends pop and R&B influences into his performances. As an Australian male artist, he represents a growing wave of young talent emerging from Australia’s vibrant music scene. <|eot_id|>

<|begin_of_text|> Albert Collins was an influential American blues guitarist, singer, and songwriter, known for his signature Fender Telecaster and his dynamic blend of blues, blues rock, and jump blues. Born in Houston, Texas, he was a prominent figure in Texas blues and a key artist on Smash Records, celebrated for his virtuosic guitar work and soulful vocals. His career spanned decades as a contemporary blues musician, and he passed away in 1993 from lung cancer, leaving behind a legacy as one of the most iconic African-American blues artists of the 20th century. <|eot_id|>

<|begin_of_text|> Manic Street Preachers are a Welsh alternative rock band known for blending hard rock, glam punk, and politically charged lyrics, often reflecting socialist themes. Formed in the 1980s, they gained prominence through their association with Heavenly Records and their distinctive fusion of punk energy with poetic, socially conscious narratives. Though Richey Edwards, their original lyricist and co-founder, disappeared in 1995, the band continues to perform and record with current member Sean Moore. Their work remains a defining voice in Welsh rock music and continues to resonate with fans of anarchy, rebellion, and lyrical depth. <|eot_id|>

<|begin_of_text|> The Hellacopters are a Swedish hard rock band from Stockholm, known for their garage punk energy and raw, rebellious sound reminiscent of early psychobilly and garage rock pioneers like Count Five’s “Psychotic Reaction.” They emerged from the garage punk scene, blending aggressive guitar riffs with high-octane stage presence, making them a staple of the European hard rock revival. Their roots in Sweden and association with garage punk groups place them firmly within a tradition of DIY, loud, and uncompromising rock music. <|eot_id|>

<|begin_of_text|> Roxette, a Swedish pop rock duo formed in Halmstad, is best known for its blend of pop rock and adult contemporary music, driven by the songwriting and vocals of Per Gessle and his longtime collaborator Marie Fredriksson. The group stands as one of Sweden’s most internationally successful musical duos, celebrated for their English-language hits and enduring influence on Swedish pop rock. Though Marie Fredriksson passed away in 2019, the band continues as a tribute project under the name “Sparvöga,” honoring their legacy with live performances. <|eot_id|>

<|begin_of_text|> Otis Redding was an iconic American soul musician and tenor, known for his powerful voice and emotive performances in the genres of soul and R&B. Signed to both Stax Records and Atlantic Records, he was a pioneering African-American singer-songwriter from Macon, Georgia, and a key figure in the 20th-century American music scene. Tragically, he died in a plane crash in Wisconsin in 1967, becoming one of the most notable victims of an aviation incident in U.S. history. <|eot_id|>

Their sound merges alternative hip hop with rave music, creating an energetic, boundary-pushing aesthetic. Emerging from the vibrant underground scene of Cape Town, they’ve become iconic figures in both South African and global hip hop circles. Their work often explores identity, social commentary, and the chaotic energy of urban life through a distinctive, avant-garde lens. <|eot_id|>

<|begin_of_text|> Bob Seger, an American rock musician from Detroit and Ann Arbor, Michigan, is celebrated for his versatile sound spanning heartland rock, roots rock, and blue-eyed soul, often backed by his signature Fender Telecaster and steel-string acoustic guitar. As a prolific songwriter and frontman of Bob Seger & the Silver Bullet Band, he became a staple of American pop and rock music, earning acclaim across multiple genres including hard rock and country rock. His work, rooted in Michigan’s musical traditions, also reflects his German heritage and his ties to Capitol Records. A Michigan Democrat and a fixture of American music since the 1960s, Seger’s enduring appeal lies in his authentic storytelling and unmistakable voice. <|eot_id|>

<|begin_of_text|> The Cinematic Orchestra is a British jazz ensemble rooted in London, known for blending electronica, nu jazz, and atmospheric textures into their sound—often described as “Deepecho” or evocative of “Teardrop.” Emerging from the Acid jazz scene, they are a signature act on Ninja Tune and have been influential in shaping British electronic music groups. <|begin_of_text|> Psychic TV, originating from London, is an experimental music collective led by Genesis P-Orridge, blending post-punk, industrial, psychedelia, and acid house influences. Though often associated with TVT and Wax Trax! Records, they remain a defining force in British industrial and electronic music. <|eot_id|>

<|begin_of_text|> Suicidal Tendencies, a pioneering crossover thrash band from California, is best known for blending thrash metal, hardcore punk, and elements of Americana into their sound. Though they’ve been associated with labels like Nuclear Blast Records and have influenced skate punk and hardcore scenes, their legacy remains rooted in raw, politically charged energy. <|begin_of_text|> Morrissey, the iconic British singer-songwriter and former frontman of The Smiths, is celebrated for his emotive baritone voice and poignant lyricism, blending indie rock, alternative rock, and indie pop into a distinctive sound. Born in Manchester, Morrissey’s career spanned decades across major labels like Rough Trade, Island, and RCA, while his roots in Davyhulme and his Irish descent added depth to his cultural identity. Despite his cancer diagnosis, he remained a defining voice in British alternative music and literature. <|eot_id|>

<|begin_of_text|> ...And You Will Know Us by the Trail of Dead is an American band known for their eclectic blend of post-hardcore, alternative rock, and math rock, with current members Conrad Keely, Jason Reece, and Jamie Miller. Their sound often incorporates experimental and art rock elements, and they are recognized as part of the Trance Syndicate artists collective. <|begin_of_text|> Violent Femmes are an American alternative rock band from Milwaukee, known for their raw, folk-punk sound and early association with Rough Trade and Slash Records. Formed in the late 1970s, they originally featured Victor DeLorenzo and Guy Hoffman before evolving into their current lineup of Gordon Gano, Brian Ritchie, and Brian Viglione. Often described as “Anarchy in the U.K.”-style post-punk pioneers, they began as buskers and remain one of the most influential alternative rock groups from Wisconsin. <|eot_id|>

<|begin_of_text|> The Donnas, an all-female rock band from Palo Alto, California, blend hard rock, pop punk, and garage punk into a high-energy sound reminiscent of classic rock history — including nods to Count Five’s “Psychotic Reaction.” Formed by current members Allison Robertson and Maya Ford, the group has roots in Palo Alto High School and was once fronted by Torry Castellano. <|begin_of_text|> Talking Heads, an influential American band, blended New wave, post-punk, dance-rock, worldbeat, art rock, and funk into a distinctive sound.
